decisions.question: (a) Should half-precision SiLU be evaluated in F32 and rounded once, as PyTorch's silu is, instead of Burn's x * sigmoid(x), which rounds the sigmoid before the product?
decisions.rationale:
This is a semantic correction against the pinned reference, and it is settled exactly at the operation level, not by a tolerance.

What the operation-level data shows (measured):
- PyTorch 2.10.0's CPU F.silu equals the F32 value x*sigmoid(x) rounded once on all 65,280 finite BF16 inputs. One F16 near-tie differs, and MPS also flushes BF16 subnormals.
- Burn's composed graph misses that once-rounded value on 27% of BF16 and F16 inputs with 2^-8 <= |x| < 16. The worst miss is 1.41 ulp in BF16 and 8 ulp in F16, where the F16 sigmoid underflows below x = -17.3.

What changes after the patch (measured):
- Block-0 SiLU equals torch's on 99.985-100% of real pre-activations, on all five checkpoints.
- On SmolLM-135M, the position-0 residual after block 0 is bit-identical to official CPU BF16.
- Position-0 logits move 10-78% closer to official BF16 on 5 of 5 checkpoints.
- Patched Burn's largest deviations land on the official graphs' own (position, token) with the same values: on Qwen3-4B, 0.7000 and 0.8795 equal CPU eager, and 0.8573 equals MPS eager and SDPA.

The mixed whole-prompt figures are not evidence against fidelity. Two moved the wrong way: Flex/BF16 SmolLM3-3B +18%, and Metal/F16 +12-21% against the single CPU-F16 eager graph. Both are distances to one official sample at t >= 1, where attention-path rounding dominates and error cancellation can go either way. Per-block agreement at position 0 improves throughout.

Logit gates cannot arbitrate a one-rounding change. Even R4 misses an injected twice-rounded SiLU on SmolLM-135M (1.445x E). The Qwen3-4B flip from pass to fail under the 1.2 rule reproduces the official MPS value exactly, so it is evidence for (b), not a defect.

Precedent: c2936fe applied the same rule to tanh GELU.

Cost (measured):
- Metal/F16 Qwen3-4B: prefill +0.8-0.9%, decode within noise, peak unchanged at 11.72 GB.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B: prefill +2% at 512 tokens.
- Flex/BF16 activation alone: +14-18%. Its end-to-end share is inferred, not measured, because the end-to-end series stopped after one round; the plan measures it.

Qwen3.5-0.8B parity stays well above its 0.999 cosine gate. Its cached minimum, however, falls from 0.999997671 to 0.999995622, and the new record must say so. If the benchmark rerun breaches the approved 5%/10% thresholds, re-baselining becomes a maintainer decision.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- Keep Burn's composed graph: it is a known deviation from the reference on 27% of gate-range inputs, against AGENTS.md's fidelity rule and the c2936fe precedent.
- Land it only once it turns gates green: gate verdicts cannot resolve one rounding, and they came from a miscalibrated rule. Exactness is the criterion.
- A custom fused CubeCL kernel: premature for a +0.9% Metal prefill cost. Revisit only if a performance gate fails.
- An opt-in flag: the reference's numerics must be the default, and the old graph has no fidelity value to preserve.
- Extending the change to ClampedSwiGlu: its reference composes operation by operation, so rounding once there would itself be a deviation.

decisions.question: (b) What prompt-logit rule replaces "1.2 times Transformers' CPU-eager BF16 deviation", given that Transformers' own other BF16 graphs fail it?
decisions.decision:
Adopt the official-graph envelope rule R4.

The envelope:
- For each prompt, E_max and E_mean are the largest max |Δ| and mean |Δ| from the truth (F32; F64 for Qwen2-7B) over the four official graphs that Transformers 5.2.0 / torch 2.10.0 run on this host in the run's dtype: CPU eager, CPU SDPA, MPS eager and MPS SDPA.
- The gate reads the four bundles at run time.

The pass condition:
- A run passes a prompt when max <= 1.5 E_max and mean <= 1.3 E_mean, both inclusive.
- Single rows (cached prefill, batched rows, chunk ends) use 1.5 E_max.

The slacks:
- They are the pooled leave-one-out (LOO) maxima of the official graphs only: 1.4206 for the max (gemma prompt 2, MPS SDPA), 1.2988 for the mean (Qwen3-4B prompt 2, CPU eager), and 1.269/1.114 for decode rows, rounded up to two significant digits.
- They become compiled constants documented with this derivation.
- They are re-derived, never tuned, whenever graphs, versions, prompts or checkpoints change.
- A bundle-only test fails if any official graph falls outside the envelope of the other three under these constants.

Pairing becomes fail-closed on graph identity. Each (device, attention_implementation) pair must appear exactly once, in the run's dtype, not --bf16-resident, all from one generator script SHA-256, and every current truth check still applies.

Exact operation-level rounding-point tests complement the logit gates. They, not the gates, are the instrument that settles (a)-type defects.
decisions.rationale:
A tolerance that rejects the reference implementation itself measures which kernel path ran, not correctness.

What the measurements show:
- Transformers' own graphs exceed CPU eager by up to 2.195x (SmolLM-135M prompt 2 mean, MPS eager).
- R0, the current rule, rejects 11 of 57 non-CPU-eager official statistics, on 5 of 7 bundles.
- Judged leave-one-out, R1 (1.0 E) rejects 23 of 76 official statistics and R2 (1.2 E) rejects 5. R3 (1.5 E) and R4 admit all 76.

Among rules that admit every official graph, R4 is the most sensitive. It flags 7 of 20 injected defects, against R3's 2:
- BF16 RMSNorm, on 3 checkpoints, up to 2.79x;
- BF16 rope angles on SmolLM-135M;
- twice-rounded SiLU on Qwen2-7B;
- softmax with BF16 intermediates on Qwen2-7B.
R0's 12 flags and R2's 8 cannot be interpreted, because those rules also fail official graphs.

Why two slacks: the max is a single-entry extreme with a heavier tail (LOO 1.42), while the mean concentrates over T x V entries (LOO 1.30).

Why the MPS graphs belong in the envelope: they are official evaluations, they are deterministic from run to run (reruns were byte-identical), and they are exactly where the 1.2 rule failed.

Rescoring existing statistics under R4, with no new runs:
- Every Burn Flex/BF16 row at 53f167b passes. The largest ratios are 1.304x on the max (SmolLM-135M prompt 1) and 1.042x on the mean.
- The patched-SiLU statistics stay within 1.18x on the max and 1.02x on the mean. The reruns must confirm this.
- Gemma Metal/F16 still fails as non-finite.

Limits, stated plainly:
- No logit-level rule can see one extra rounding, because the official graphs themselves spread 1.42x / 1.30x leave-one-out.
- A LOO maximum over 76 samples leaves an exchangeable new implementation roughly a 1-in-77 chance per statistic of exceeding it. An exceedance is therefore a finding to diagnose with per-block dumps and operation-level comparison. It is never an automatic defect verdict and never a reason to widen the rule.
- The mean slack has only 0.09% headroom over its derivation. That is why re-derivation is mandatory whenever the inputs change.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- R0 (current), R1 and R2: they reject Transformers' own graphs.
- R3 (1.5 for both statistics): it admits every official graph but loses the mean's sensitivity (2 of 20 defects).
- A slack on a single bundle: covering the official graphs from CPU eager alone needs 2.2, which removes all sensitivity.
- A CPU-only envelope for the Flex profile: an arbitrary narrowing. The device is not what separates correct from incorrect rounding.
- Dispersion rules such as E + k·sigma: with four graphs, sigma cannot be estimated.
- Per-position or position-0-split envelopes: probably sharper at t >= 1 on checkpoints dominated by position 0 (SmolLM3-3B, Qwen2-7B), but their leave-one-out slack has not been derived. This is an offline follow-up from the existing bundles.
- Any slack derived from Burn's own statistics, including gpt-oss's 1.1725, the basis of the current 1.2: Burn data is a forbidden calibration source.

implementation.evidence: R4 with the derived slacks BF16 1.5/1.3 (envelope record, derivation); the operation-level rounding-point tests (3cf845f) found and fixed the eager attention scale (edf4cf0). This rerun's bundle-only leave-one-out tests pass for every calibrated truth at 8181605.

decisions.question: (b, F16 profile) How should a Metal/F16 run be calibrated, given that the generator wrote no F16 bundles and the BF16 bounds were reused as an upper limit?
decisions.rationale:
The BF16 bounds neither reflect F16's 8x finer unit roundoff nor detect range failures.

No fixed scale exists between the two dtypes (measured): on gpt-oss, Metal/F16 reached 0.007-0.874 of the BF16 statistics. Dividing the BF16 envelope by 8 would be an inferred model that this spread contradicts.

The Qwen2-7B case (measured):
- Metal/F16 sits at 0.18-1.15x of the BF16 envelope, where F16 should be far finer.
- Its prompt rows at t >= 1 err by 1.4-2.2, while Flex/BF16 errs by 0.11-0.16.
- Its decode rows reach 3.546 max / 0.3775 mean, which is 1.68x / 1.33x even of the BF16 envelope.
- Its self-consistency gap is exactly 0, and the BF16 proxy passes it.

Precedent: the crate already calibrates Nemotron-H's Burn F16 against official F16 evaluations.

Why all four F16 graphs must be finite: when one official graph overflows, F16 evaluation of that checkpoint is range-marginal, and a finite Burn result there reflects kernel luck, not fidelity.

Expect further findings once F16 envelopes exist. One hint, inferred and not measured: Llama-3.1-8B's Metal/F16 maximum is the same 0.1038 on all three prompts, 0.49-0.72 of the BF16 envelope. Any such results are findings, not reasons to widen.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- Keep the BF16 proxy: it is lenient and cannot see F16-specific defects, as Qwen2-7B shows.
- Scale the BF16 envelope by 2^-3: an inferred model that gpt-oss's 0.007-0.874 ratios contradict.
- Build the envelope only from the finite F16 graphs: that would certify range-marginal evaluation.
- Borrow BF16's slacks for F16: the cross-graph spread is a property of each dtype, so it must be derived from F16 data.

implementation.evidence: F16 slacks 1.7/1.7 from the official F16 graphs (envelope record); Qwen2-7B fails as uncalibrated in F16 here too (3 gates, 2 calibration tests), and gemma-3-4b-it has no F16 envelope.

decisions.question: (c) What replaces the 0.5 decode self-consistency bound, which Transformers' own BF16 cached decode exceeds (by up to 1.75)?
decisions.decision:
Use truth-anchored decode rows under the same envelope rule.

Truth rows and envelope:
- Each truth gets decode rows: F32 CPU-eager stateless logits at the truth's teacher-forced greedy positions. These come from the round-2 f32-cpu-eager bundles, which are byte-identical to their truths; Qwen2-7B gets a new F64 decode truth.
- E_dec,max and E_dec,mean are the largest deviations of the four official graphs' cached and stateless rows from those truth rows.

Pass condition:
- Burn's cached decode rows, and its stateless rows at the same positions, must each satisfy max <= 1.5 E_dec,max and mean <= 1.3 E_dec,mean, using the pooled slacks.
- The cached-versus-stateless gap is then bounded by 3 E_dec,max by the triangle inequality, so it is printed as a diagnostic only.

Related checks:
- The decoded-longest-prompt check is judged against an envelope built from the official graphs' own cached decode under the gate's quarter-prefill protocol, not against the stateless envelope.
- A greedy step is decisive when the truth margin exceeds twice max(1.5 E_max of prompt 0, 1.5 E_dec,max).
- F32 runs additionally compare their cached decode rows with the decode truth at their existing F32 tolerance.

Scope:
- The other uses of 0.5 stay as explicitly provisional, uncalibrated checks: cached prefill, batched rows, and Gemma long chunk ends. They stay until the generator records the official graphs' own batched and chunked rows.
- Gemma long's 8 post-wrap decode steps move to truth-anchored rows now.
decisions.rationale:
Why 0.5 cannot stay:
- It rejects 14 of 28 official runs, on 5 of 7 checkpoints (Qwen2-7B CPU eager 1.75, gemma MPS eager 1.5625).
- Official F32 decode, by contrast, stays at or below 2.6e-4.
- So the gap belongs to a pair of kernel paths, not to the precision: CPU-eager BF16 is often exactly 0, while SDPA and MPS reach 1.56.

No gap-based bound can be calibrated:
- W, judged leave-one-out, rejects 4 of 28 official runs.
- 1.2W rejects 1 official run, plus Burn's gemma c2936fe dump (2.25 > 1.875).
- A bound from the CPU-eager twin's own gap would be 0 on SmolLM-135M.
- The prompt-derived 2·s·M0 is vacuous on Qwen2-7B (20), SmolLM3-3B (15) and gemma-long (19), and too tight on gemma (0.92 against the official 1.56).
- The triangle bound 2 × 1.2 × E_ce admits every official run, but catches off-by-one rope only on Llama-3.1-8B and on 3 of 4 SmolLM-135M graphs.

What truth-anchored rows admit:
- Every official graph: decode LOO 1.269 / 1.114, below 1.5 / 1.3.
- Every Burn Flex/BF16 fused dump. The largest are Llama-3.1-8B at 1.26x, and the gemma c2936fe step-13 cached row at 2.153 (1.42x), whose 6% margin needs a targeted look.

What they catch:
- Off-by-one rope, dropped keys and FP8 KV caches on SmolLM-135M, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2-7B, except off-by-one rope on Qwen2-7B MPS SDPA (0.62x mean).
- Defects that self-consistency cannot see at all: Qwen2-7B Metal/F16 (gap 0; rows at 1.68x / 1.33x) and Burn's non-default Flex/BF16 eager attention on Qwen3-4B (mean 1.48x).

Why the decoded-longest-prompt check needs its own envelope: on SmolLM-135M, the official MPS cached quarter-prefill decode reaches 1.601 against a stateless E_max of 1.101 (1.45x).

Why the greedy threshold must use the bound of the rows it compares: the decode envelope exceeds the prompt-0 envelope on gemma (1.519 against 0.384) and on Llama-3.1-8B (0.231 against 0.137).

F32 stays the high-resolution check of cache and position logic: off-by-one rope gives at least 1.2, against 2.6e-4. Today, however, the F32 gates compare only argmaxes on decode steps, which is why the F32 decode-row check is added.

No official measurement exists for the remaining uses of 0.5, and Burn measured 0 to 0.0625 there. Labeling them provisional is honest; widening or removing them without data would not be.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- Keep 0.5: it rejects half of the official runs.
- W or 1.2W: they reject official graphs and Burn's gemma run.
- The twin's own gap: it is 0 on SmolLM-135M.
- 2·s·M0: vacuous on some checkpoints and too tight on gemma.
- The 2 × 1.2 × E_ce triangle bound: less sensitive than truth-anchored rows.
- Drop decode checks: a broken half-precision decode would then pass wherever no greedy step is decisive.
- Replace the batched, cached-prefill and chunk-end 0.5 now: no official data exists for them, so that would be inferred calibration.

implementation.evidence: Truth-anchored decode rows judge every half-precision cached greedy gate of this rerun; the F32 runs print their new decode-truth rows (pre_silu.new_statistic_lines); 0.5 remains only as the provisional tolerance of cached prefills, batched rows, and Gemma's long chunk ends.

decisions.question: (d) What should the crate do for Gemma 3 at F16, given that the published checkpoints overflow F16 in Transformers too and the crate returns NaN logits?
decisions.decision:
Refuse F16 loads of Gemma 3 checkpoints (model_type gemma3 and gemma3_text) by default, with a contextual error. Offer an explicit opt-in that runs the faithful graph, which reproduces the reference's overflow, for experiments.

Do not clamp.

Gate changes:
- Drop the Metal/F16 Gemma gate profile.
- Keep Metal/F32 as Metal's Gemma qualification.
- Keep Flex/BF16, and CUDA BF16, as Gemma's half-precision profiles.

Implement the refusal as a family-declared range hazard checked by a generic LoadOptions policy, not as a model-name branch in shared code.
decisions.rationale:
Where F16 overflows (measured):
- In 4B, the first F16 overflow is at block 5 of 34: the residual addition after the MLP, at the BOS position, channel 443. The sum is 51,941.5 + 21,568.1 = 73,509.6, 12% above F16's 65,504.
- It is identical in torch CPU and MPS F16 and in Burn Metal and Flex F16.
- 12B overflows at block 6 (83,968) and 27B at block 8 (83,456).
- Residual peaks reach 3.0e5 to 8.9e5.
- Non-initial positions also exceed the range: blocks 27-33 in 4B, and from block 10 on the 1237-token prompt.
- Without BOS the overflow still occurs, at block 30.
So any faithful F16 evaluation overflows. That is inferred for any device, and measured on CPU, MPS and Burn.

The cause: every branch tensor fits F16 in 4B. The overflow comes from one channel whose post-norm gain |1+w| reaches 1,369, combined with the BOS massive activation.

Why refuse rather than return NaN:
- Silent NaN violates AGENTS.md's requirement of contextual errors for unsupported capabilities, and the generation processors assume finite or -inf logits.
- The crate already refuses an unreferenced final soft-cap rather than silently changing logits.

Why not clamp: the T5-style clamp gives finite logits but a different model. At positions >= 1 the max |Δ| is 10.5-19.7 and the mean 1.10-1.54, against official BF16's 0.38-0.75 and 0.041-0.069, and argmax changes. An F32 run with the same clamp deviates just as much, so the error comes from the clamp.

Why not refuse outright: a hard refusal would block legitimate experiments, such as truncated stacks (4B blocks 0-4 are finite), studying the overflow, and interventions.

Gemma 3 1B and 270m are unmeasured. The family-wide refusal is a default policy, and the error message must separate measured sizes from unmeasured ones.

This is a policy choice. The maintainer should confirm the default, its scope (family-wide or measured sizes only), and the API shape.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- Status quo (silent NaN): rejected for the reasons above.
- Unconditional refusal: blocks legitimate experiments.
- Clamp by default: the reference has no clamp for Gemma 3, and the clamped model deviates materially.
- Keep the residual stream in F32 as mixed precision: no official counterpart exists to calibrate it. It could become a future explicit experimental profile.
- Runtime finiteness checks in forward: a device sync on every call, and an API change for every family. A cheap non-finite guard in generation, where logits are already read back, is a separate maintainer option.
- Refuse only the exact measured revisions: brittle, and it misses fine-tunes.
- Qualify Metal in BF16 instead: impossible on Burn 0.21 (next decision).

implementation.status: least invasive variant only (gate-level refusal); the library-level policy awaits the maintainer
implementation.evidence: The gates refuse TRANSFORMERS_GEMMA_DTYPE=f16 (all five Metal Gemma gates in this rerun); the plan's S7 (RangeHazardPolicy in LoadOptions, a family-declared hazard, and its tests) was not implemented, because the decision is flagged for user review. The library still evaluates the faithful, overflowing F16 graph.

decisions.question: (d, Metal BF16) Can Metal be qualified in BF16 instead, and should the crate patch CubeCL or upgrade Burn for it?
decisions.decision:
Not on the pinned Burn 0.21.
- Do not declare BF16 in a local CubeCL patch.
- Keep the existing contextual refusal ("backend cannot store checkpoint dtype BF16").
- Record the probe in the new measurement record.
- Revisit at a Burn >= 0.22 upgrade. That upgrade is a separate maintainer decision: it raises the MSRV from 1.92 to at least 1.95 and requires migrating to the backend-erased Tensor API.
decisions.rationale:
What fails on Burn 0.21 / CubeCL 0.10 (measured):
- The device reports supports_dtype(BF16) = false.
- MSL for exp, tanh, sqrt and cos does not compile, because Metal's math functions have no bfloat overloads.
- The compile failure panics wgpu's device thread while the caller gets garbage back: exp is off by up to 50.6 and softmax returns near-zero rows.
- cubek-matmul refuses BF16.

Patching CubeCL 0.10 to declare BF16 makes storage and matmul work, but leaves 34-68 shader failures per pass, and all 5 gates return non-finite logits.

Burn 0.22, tested in a standalone probe, passes every step: math functions within 0.99 u, softmax error 9.7e-5, matmul within 0.203·u·Σ|a||b|. It needs rustc >= 1.95 and a breaking API change.

Why the upgrade matters: 27B on a 96 GB Mac needs BF16, since F32 (about 108 GB) does not fit.
decisions.alternatives_rejected:
- A local CubeCL patch: kernels that silently fail to compile and return garbage are worse than a refusal.
- Emulate BF16 on Metal with F32 storage: those are not BF16 numerics, and the memory benefit is lost.
- Upgrade Burn inside this change: out of scope, and it is an MSRV and dependency policy decision.
